rules.rule_name: Open Required Business Files to Begin Billing
rules.rule_description: Before any billing activity can begin, the system must have access to all three required data sources: the Usage File (containing consumption records), the Customer File (containing customer master data), and the Invoice File (where generated invoices will be written).
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Open USAGE, CUSTOMER & INVOICE Files

acceptance_criteria.Given: The billing process is initiated
acceptance_criteria.When: The system starts the billing run
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must open the Usage File for reading, the Customer File for reading, and the Invoice File for writing before any billing records are processed

rules.rule_name: Read Usage Record to Drive Billing Cycle
rules.rule_description: The billing process is driven by usage records. Each usage record contains the customer identifier, the number of units consumed, and the billing month. The system reads one usage record at a time and uses it as the basis for generating a customer invoice.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: 1:Read Usage Record

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Usage File is open and available for reading
acceptance_criteria.When: The system reads the next usage record from the Usage File
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system captures the Customer ID, Usage Units, and Billing Month from the usage record and uses these values for all subsequent billing calculations for that customer

rules.rule_name: Detect End of Usage File to Terminate Billing Loop
rules.rule_description: The billing process must continue processing usage records until all records in the Usage File have been processed. When no more usage records exist, the billing cycle ends.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: End of Usage File?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system is in the billing processing loop reading usage records
acceptance_criteria.When: A read attempt is made on the Usage File
acceptance_criteria.Then: If there are more records, the system proceeds to find the customer and generate a bill; if there are no more records (end of file), the system exits the billing loop and proceeds to close all files and display the completion message

rules.rule_name: Locate Customer Record in Customer Master
rules.rule_description: For each usage record read, the system must locate the corresponding customer in the Customer Master File using the Customer ID from the usage record. The Customer Master File is searched from the beginning for every usage record to ensure the correct customer data is retrieved.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: 2:Find Customer

acceptance_criteria.Given: A usage record has been read with a specific Customer ID
acceptance_criteria.When: The system searches the Customer Master File
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system scans the Customer Master File from the beginning, comparing each customer record's Customer ID against the Customer ID from the usage record, and marks the customer as found when a match is identified; if no match is found after scanning all records, the customer is marked as not found

rules.rule_name: Handle Customer Not Found in Customer Master
rules.rule_description: If a usage record references a Customer ID that does not exist in the Customer Master File, the system cannot generate an invoice. The error must be logged and the system must continue processing the next usage record.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Log Error: Customer Not Found

acceptance_criteria.Given: A usage record has been read with a specific Customer ID
acceptance_criteria.When: The Customer ID from the usage record does not match any record in the Customer Master File
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system logs the error message 'ERROR: CUSTOMER NOT FOUND' along with the unmatched Customer ID, skips invoice generation for this usage record, and proceeds to read the next usage record

rules.rule_name: Validate Customer Active Status Before Billing
rules.rule_description: Only customers with an ACTIVE status are eligible to receive invoices. The customer status must be validated after the customer record is found in the Customer Master File.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: 3:Validate Customer Status

acceptance_criteria.Given: A customer record has been found in the Customer Master File matching the Customer ID from the usage record
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates the customer's status field
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the customer status is 'ACTIVE', the system proceeds to calculate the bill and generate an invoice; if the customer status is anything other than 'ACTIVE', the system logs an error and skips invoice generation for this customer

rules.rule_name: Handle Inactive Customer — Skip Invoice Generation
rules.rule_description: If a customer exists in the Customer Master File but their status is not ACTIVE, the system must not generate an invoice. The error must be logged and the system must continue processing the next usage record.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Log Error: Customer Is Not Active

acceptance_criteria.Given: A customer record has been found in the Customer Master File
acceptance_criteria.When: The customer's status is not 'ACTIVE'
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system logs the error message 'ERROR: CUSTOMER IS NOT ACTIVE' along with the Customer ID, skips all billing calculations and invoice generation for this usage record, and proceeds to read the next usage record

rules.rule_name: Determine Per-Unit Rate Based on Usage Tier
rules.rule_description: The per-unit billing rate is determined by the total number of units consumed in the billing period. Three pricing tiers exist, and the applicable rate is a single flat rate applied to all units based on which tier the total consumption falls into.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
4:Determine Usage Rate
Tier 1: ≤500 units @ $0.50
Tier 2: 501-1000 units @ $0.45
Tier 3: >1000 units @ $0.40

acceptance_criteria.Given: An active customer's usage record is being processed with a known number of usage units
acceptance_criteria.When: The system determines the applicable billing rate
acceptance_criteria.Then: If usage units are 500 or fewer, the rate is set to $0.50 per unit; if usage units are between 501 and 1000 (inclusive), the rate is set to $0.45 per unit; if usage units exceed 1000, the rate is set to $0.40 per unit — the selected rate applies to all units consumed

rules.rule_name: Calculate Usage Charge from Units and Rate
rules.rule_description: The base usage charge is calculated by multiplying the total units consumed by the applicable per-unit rate determined from the pricing tier.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
5:Calculate Usage Charge
Units × Rate

acceptance_criteria.Given: The usage units and the applicable per-unit rate have been determined
acceptance_criteria.When: The system calculates the usage charge
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Usage Charge is computed as: Usage Units multiplied by the Per-Unit Rate

rules.rule_name: Apply Volume Discount When Usage Exceeds Threshold
rules.rule_description: Customers whose usage exceeds the defined volume threshold qualify for a volume discount. The discount is calculated as a percentage of the usage charge and reduces the amount the customer owes.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Units > 1000
Volume Threshold?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The usage charge has been calculated for an active customer
acceptance_criteria.When: The system checks whether the customer's usage units exceed the Volume Threshold
acceptance_criteria.Then: If usage units are greater than the Volume Threshold, a Volume Discount is calculated as the Usage Charge multiplied by the Volume Discount Rate and stored as the discount amount; if usage units do not exceed the Volume Threshold, no volume discount is applied and the discount amount remains zero

rules.rule_name: Apply Additional Premium Customer Discount
rules.rule_description: Customers classified as PREMIUM receive an additional discount on top of any volume discount already applied. This premium discount is calculated as a percentage of the original usage charge and is added to the existing discount amount.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
7:Apply Premium Customer Discount
Additional 5% off Usage Charge

acceptance_criteria.Given: The usage charge has been calculated and any applicable volume discount has been determined
acceptance_criteria.When: The system checks whether the customer type is 'PREMIUM'
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the customer type is 'PREMIUM', the Premium Discount is calculated as the Usage Charge multiplied by the Premium Discount Rate, and this amount is added to any existing discount (volume discount); the total discount becomes: existing discount plus premium discount; if the customer type is not 'PREMIUM', no additional premium discount is applied

rules.rule_name: Enforce Minimum Charge Floor on Taxable Amount
rules.rule_description: To ensure the business always recovers a baseline revenue amount, a minimum charge floor is enforced. If the net charge after all discounts falls below the minimum charge, the taxable amount is set to the minimum charge instead.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
8:Apply Minimum Charge Rule
Minimum Charge = $25.00

acceptance_criteria.Given: The usage charge and all applicable discounts have been calculated
acceptance_criteria.When: The system computes the net charge by subtracting total discounts from the usage charge
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the net charge (Usage Charge minus Total Discount) is less than the Minimum Charge of $25.00, the Taxable Amount is set to $25.00; otherwise, the Taxable Amount is set to the net charge (Usage Charge minus Total Discount)

rules.rule_name: Calculate Tax Using Customer-Specific Tax Rate
rules.rule_description: Tax is calculated on the taxable amount using the individual customer's tax rate stored in the Customer Master record. Each customer may have a different tax rate, reflecting their applicable tax jurisdiction or classification.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
9:Calculate Tax
Taxable Amount × Customer Tax Rate

acceptance_criteria.Given: The taxable amount has been determined after applying discounts and the minimum charge rule
acceptance_criteria.When: The system calculates the tax for the invoice
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Tax Amount is computed as: Taxable Amount multiplied by the Customer's Tax Rate (retrieved from the Customer Master record)

rules.rule_name: Calculate Final Invoice Amount Including Previous Balance
rules.rule_description: The final amount due on the invoice includes the current period's taxable charge, the tax amount, and any outstanding previous balance carried forward from the customer's account.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
10:Calculate Final Invoice Amount
Taxable Amount + Tax + Previous Balance

acceptance_criteria.Given: The taxable amount and tax amount have been calculated, and the customer's previous balance is available from the Customer Master record
acceptance_criteria.When: The system calculates the final invoice amount
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Final Invoice Amount is computed as: Taxable Amount plus Tax Amount plus Customer's Previous Balance

rules.rule_name: Generate Unique Invoice Number from Billing Month and Customer ID
rules.rule_description: Each invoice must have a unique identifier that ties it to a specific billing period and customer. The invoice number is constructed by combining the billing month from the usage record and the customer ID.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
11:Generate Invoice Number
Billing Month + Customer ID

acceptance_criteria.Given: The billing month from the usage record and the customer ID from the Customer Master are available
acceptance_criteria.When: The system generates the invoice number
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Invoice Number is constructed by concatenating the Billing Month, a hyphen separator '-', and the Customer ID (format: BILLING-MONTH-CUSTOMERID)

rules.rule_name: Format All Monetary Values for Invoice Output
rules.rule_description: Before writing the invoice record, all monetary values must be formatted into their display representation to ensure the invoice output is correctly structured and readable.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
12:Format Invoice Output
Format all monetary values

acceptance_criteria.Given: All billing calculations have been completed including usage charge, discount, tax, previous balance, and final amount
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares the invoice record for output
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system formats the Usage Charge, Total Discount, Tax Amount, Previous Balance, and Final Amount into their display formats, then assembles a pipe-delimited output record containing: Invoice Number, Customer ID, Customer Name, Usage Units, Formatted Usage Charge, Formatted Discount, Formatted Tax, Formatted Previous Balance, and Formatted Final Amount — in that order

rules.rule_name: Write Completed Invoice Record to Invoice File
rules.rule_description: Once the invoice has been fully calculated and formatted, the invoice record must be written to the Invoice File and a confirmation message displayed to acknowledge successful invoice generation.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: 13:Write Invoice Record

acceptance_criteria.Given: The invoice output record has been fully formatted with all required fields
acceptance_criteria.When: The system writes the invoice
acceptance_criteria.Then: The formatted invoice record is written to the Invoice File, and the system displays the confirmation message 'INVOICE GENERATED:' followed by the Invoice Number

rules.rule_name: Close All Files and Confirm Billing Process Completion
rules.rule_description: Once all usage records have been processed, the billing run must be formally concluded by closing all open files and displaying a completion message to confirm the billing process has finished successfully.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
14:Billing Process Completion
Close All Files & Display Completion Message

acceptance_criteria.Given: All usage records in the Usage File have been processed
acceptance_criteria.When: The end of the Usage File is reached and the billing loop exits
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system closes the Customer File, Usage File, and Invoice File, then displays the completion message 'BILL01 BILLING PROCESS COMPLETE' and terminates the billing process

rules.rule_name: Read Next Usage Record from Usage File
rules.rule_description: The billing system reads each customer usage record sequentially from the Usage File (USAGE.dat) to retrieve billing data for processing.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Read Next Record from Usage File

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Usage File (USAGE.dat) is open and available for reading, and the billing process has been initiated or a previous usage record has already been processed
acceptance_criteria.When: The system attempts to read the next sequential record from the Usage File
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system retrieves the next available usage record containing the customer's usage data for the billing period

rules.rule_name: Detect End of Usage File to Stop Processing
rules.rule_description: When no more usage records exist in the Usage File, the billing process must recognize the end-of-file condition and stop processing further records.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Record Available?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system is reading records sequentially from the Usage File
acceptance_criteria.When: The system attempts to read a record and no more records are available in the Usage File (end-of-file condition is reached)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the End-of-Usage indicator to TRUE, which terminates the main billing processing loop and no further usage records are processed

rules.rule_name: Capture Customer ID from Usage Record
rules.rule_description: When a valid usage record is successfully read, the Customer ID from the usage record must be captured as the current customer being billed, so it can be used to look up the customer in the Customer Master.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Capture Customer ID

acceptance_criteria.Given: A usage record has been successfully read from the Usage File and a record is available (not end-of-file)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system processes the successfully read usage record
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Customer ID field from the usage record (USAGE-CUST-ID) is captured and stored as the current Customer ID (WS-CURRENT-CUSTOMER-ID) to be used for customer lookup and invoice generation

rules.rule_name: Capture Number of Units Consumed from Usage Record
rules.rule_description: When a valid usage record is successfully read, the number of units consumed by the customer must be captured from the usage record, as it drives rate tier selection, discount eligibility, and charge calculation.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Capture Number of Units Consumed

acceptance_criteria.Given: A usage record has been successfully read from the Usage File and a record is available (not end-of-file)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system processes the successfully read usage record
acceptance_criteria.Then: The units consumed field from the usage record (USAGE-UNITS) is captured and stored as the current usage units (WS-USAGE-UNITS) to be used in billing calculations including rate determination, volume discount eligibility, and usage charge computation

rules.rule_name: Capture Billing Month from Usage Record
rules.rule_description: When a valid usage record is successfully read, the billing month must be captured from the usage record, as it identifies the period for which the customer is being billed and is used to construct the invoice number.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Capture Billing Month

acceptance_criteria.Given: A usage record has been successfully read from the Usage File and a record is available (not end-of-file)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system processes the successfully read usage record
acceptance_criteria.Then: The billing month field from the usage record (USAGE-MONTH) is captured and stored as the current billing month (WS-BILLING-MONTH) to be used for invoice number generation in the format [BILLING-MONTH]-[CUSTOMER-ID]

rules.rule_name: Usage Record Ready for Billing Processing
rules.rule_description: Only when all three required data elements — Customer ID, Units Consumed, and Billing Month — have been successfully captured from a usage record is the record considered complete and ready to proceed to customer lookup and bill calculation.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: End: Usage Record Ready for Processing

acceptance_criteria.Given: A usage record has been successfully read from the Usage File (not end-of-file)
acceptance_criteria.When: All three data elements have been captured: the Customer ID (WS-CURRENT-CUSTOMER-ID), the number of units consumed (WS-USAGE-UNITS), and the billing month (WS-BILLING-MONTH)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The usage record is considered fully prepared and the billing process proceeds to the next step of locating the corresponding customer in the Customer Master file using the captured Customer ID

rules.rule_name: Reset Customer Search State Before Each Lookup
rules.rule_description: Before searching for a customer, the system must reset the customer search state to ensure no carry-over from a previous search affects the current lookup result.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Reset Customer Search
Set Customer Found = No

acceptance_criteria.Given: A new usage record has been read and a customer lookup is about to begin
acceptance_criteria.When: The Find Customer process is initiated for the current usage record's Customer ID
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Customer Found indicator must be reset to 'No' (N) and the End-of-Customer-File indicator must be reset to 'No' (N), ensuring a clean search state before scanning the Customer Master file

rules.rule_name: Reposition Customer File to Beginning for Each Search
rules.rule_description: The Customer Master file must always be searched from the very beginning for each usage record, ensuring every customer record is eligible to be matched regardless of where the previous search ended.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Position to Beginning
of Customer File

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Customer Found indicator has been reset to 'No' and a customer lookup is about to begin for the current Customer ID from the usage record
acceptance_criteria.When: The Find Customer process positions to the start of the Customer Master file
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Customer Master file is closed and immediately reopened so that the next read will start from the first record in the file, guaranteeing a full file scan from the beginning

rules.rule_name: Read Customer Records Sequentially During Search
rules.rule_description: The system reads customer records one at a time from the Customer Master file in sequential order to find a matching customer for the current usage record.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Read Next Customer Record
from CUSTOMER.dat

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Customer Master file is open and positioned at the current read location, and neither a matching customer has been found nor the end of the file has been reached
acceptance_criteria.When: The system reads the next available customer record from the Customer Master file
acceptance_criteria.Then: The next customer record is retrieved and made available for Customer ID comparison; if no more records exist, the End-of-Customer-File indicator is set to 'True'

rules.rule_name: Detect End of Customer File During Search
rules.rule_description: When all customer records have been read without finding a match, the system must recognize that the customer does not exist in the Customer Master file and terminate the search.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
End of
Customer File?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system is sequentially reading through the Customer Master file searching for a matching Customer ID
acceptance_criteria.When: The system attempts to read the next customer record and there are no more records remaining in the Customer Master file
acceptance_criteria.Then: The End-of-Customer-File indicator is set to 'True', the search loop is terminated, and control returns to the calling process with Customer Found = 'No', indicating the customer does not exist in the Customer Master file

rules.rule_name: Match Customer Record by Customer ID
rules.rule_description: Each customer record read from the Customer Master file must be evaluated to determine whether its Customer ID matches the Customer ID from the current usage record being processed.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Customer ID Matches
Current Usage Customer ID?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A customer record has been successfully read from the Customer Master file and the End-of-Customer-File indicator is 'No'
acceptance_criteria.When: The Customer ID field (CUST-ID) from the current Customer Master record is compared against the Customer ID (WS-CURRENT-CUSTOMER-ID) extracted from the current usage record
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the two Customer IDs are equal, the customer is considered matched and the Customer Found indicator is set to 'True'; if they are not equal, the system reads the next customer record and repeats the comparison

rules.rule_name: Mark Customer as Found Upon Successful ID Match
rules.rule_description: When a customer record in the Customer Master file has a Customer ID that matches the usage record's Customer ID, the system must flag the customer as found and stop further searching.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Mark Customer as FOUND

acceptance_criteria.Given: A customer record has been read from the Customer Master file and its Customer ID exactly matches the Customer ID from the current usage record
acceptance_criteria.When: The Customer ID comparison confirms a match between CUST-ID and WS-CURRENT-CUSTOMER-ID
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Customer Found indicator is set to 'True', the search loop is immediately terminated, and the matched customer's full record (including CUST-ID, CUST-NAME, CUST-STATUS, CUST-TYPE, CUST-TAX-RATE, CUST-PREV-BALANCE) is retained in memory and returned to the calling process for use in billing

rules.rule_name: Return Customer Found Result to Billing Process
rules.rule_description: Upon successfully locating a matching customer record, the Find Customer process concludes and signals to the main billing process that the customer was found, enabling billing to proceed.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
End: Return Customer
Found = Yes

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Customer Found indicator has been set to 'True' after a successful Customer ID match in the Customer Master file
acceptance_criteria.When: The Find Customer search loop terminates because the Customer Found condition is 'True'
acceptance_criteria.Then: Control returns to the main billing process with Customer Found = 'Yes', and the full customer record data is available for subsequent status validation and bill calculation

rules.rule_name: Return Customer Not Found Result to Billing Process
rules.rule_description: When the entire Customer Master file has been scanned without finding a matching Customer ID, the Find Customer process concludes and signals to the main billing process that the customer does not exist, preventing invoice generation.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
End: Return Customer
Found = No

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has read through all records in the Customer Master file without finding a Customer ID that matches the current usage record's Customer ID
acceptance_criteria.When: The End-of-Customer-File indicator is set to 'True' and the search loop terminates
acceptance_criteria.Then: Control returns to the main billing process with Customer Found = 'No', which will cause the main process to display the error message 'ERROR: CUSTOMER NOT FOUND - [Customer ID]' and skip bill calculation and invoice generation for this usage record

rules.rule_name: Customer Existence Validation Before Billing
rules.rule_description: Before any billing activity is performed, the system must verify that the Customer ID from the usage record matches an existing customer in the Customer Master. If no matching customer is found, billing is skipped and an error is logged with the unmatched Customer ID.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Was Customer Found?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A usage record has been read with a specific Customer ID, and a search of the Customer Master file has been completed for that Customer ID
acceptance_criteria.When: No matching customer record is found in the Customer Master file for the given Customer ID
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must: (1) Log an error message 'ERROR: CUSTOMER NOT FOUND - [Customer ID]' identifying the unrecognized Customer ID, (2) Skip all billing processing (no bill calculation, no invoice generation) for this usage record, and (3) Proceed to the next usage record

rules.rule_name: Active Customer Status Validation Before Billing
rules.rule_description: Even when a customer is found in the Customer Master, billing may only proceed if that customer holds an ACTIVE status. Customers with any status other than ACTIVE are ineligible for bill generation, and an error is logged with their Customer ID.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Customer Status = ACTIVE?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A usage record has been read with a specific Customer ID, and the customer has been successfully located in the Customer Master file
acceptance_criteria.When: The customer's status in the Customer Master is NOT equal to 'ACTIVE' (i.e., the customer is inactive or holds any other non-active status)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must: (1) Log an error message 'ERROR: CUSTOMER IS NOT ACTIVE - [Customer ID]' identifying the inactive customer, (2) Skip all billing processing (no bill calculation, no invoice generation) for this usage record, and (3) Proceed to the next usage record

rules.rule_name: Proceed to Billing for Active Customers
rules.rule_description: When a customer is both found in the Customer Master and confirmed to have an ACTIVE status, the system is authorized to proceed with full billing processing — calculating the bill and generating the invoice.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Proceed to Calculate Bill & Generate Invoice

acceptance_criteria.Given: A usage record has been read with a specific Customer ID, the customer has been successfully located in the Customer Master file, and the customer's status is 'ACTIVE'
acceptance_criteria.When: Both the customer existence check and the active status check pass successfully
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must proceed to: (1) Execute the bill calculation process for the customer's usage record, and (2) Execute the invoice generation process to produce and write the invoice output

rules.rule_name: Skip Billing and Log Error for Not-Found Customer
rules.rule_description: When a Customer ID from a usage record cannot be matched to any record in the Customer Master file, the system logs a descriptive error message that includes the unmatched Customer ID, ensuring the issue is traceable, and skips billing for that record.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Log Error: Customer Not Found
Customer ID is Logged

acceptance_criteria.Given: A usage record exists with a Customer ID that was searched in the Customer Master file
acceptance_criteria.When: The Customer ID from the usage record does not match any Customer ID in the Customer Master file
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must display the error message 'ERROR: CUSTOMER NOT FOUND - [Customer ID]' where [Customer ID] is the exact Customer ID from the usage record that could not be matched, and no bill calculation or invoice generation is performed for this usage record

rules.rule_name: Skip Billing and Log Error for Inactive Customer
rules.rule_description: When a customer is found in the Customer Master but their status is not ACTIVE, the system logs a descriptive error message that includes the Customer ID of the inactive customer, ensuring the issue is traceable, and skips billing for that record.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Log Error: Customer Is Not Active
Customer ID is Logged

acceptance_criteria.Given: A usage record exists with a Customer ID that was found in the Customer Master file
acceptance_criteria.When: The customer's status field in the Customer Master record is not equal to 'ACTIVE'
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must display the error message 'ERROR: CUSTOMER IS NOT ACTIVE - [Customer ID]' where [Customer ID] is the exact Customer ID of the inactive customer, and no bill calculation or invoice generation is performed for this usage record

key_functionalities.title: Determine Usage Rate
key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    A([Start: Determine Usage Rate])
    B{Units Consumed\n≤ 500?}
    C[Assign Rate = $0.50 per unit\nTier 1 - Low Usage]
    D{Units Consumed\n≤ 1000?}
    E[Assign Rate = $0.45 per unit\nTier 2 - Medium Usage]
    F[Assign Rate = $0.40 per unit\nTier 3 - High Usage\nMore than 1000 units]
    G([End: Rate Assigned\nProceed to Calculate Usage Charge])

    A --> B
    B -->|Yes - Up to 500 Units| C
    B -->|No| D

rules.rule_name: Assign Tier 1 Low Usage Rate for Up to 500 Units
rules.rule_description: When a customer's usage units consumed in the billing period are 500 or fewer, the system assigns the Tier 1 low-usage per-unit billing rate of $0.50. This rate will be used to calculate the total usage charge for the invoice.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Assign Rate = $0.50 per unit
Tier 1 - Low Usage

acceptance_criteria.Given: A customer usage record has been read with a valid Units Consumed value, and the billing rate calculation process has been initiated for that customer
acceptance_criteria.When: The Units Consumed in the billing period is less than or equal to 500 units
acceptance_criteria.Then: The per-unit billing rate is set to $0.50 (Tier 1 - Low Usage), and the system proceeds to calculate the Usage Charge using this rate

rules.rule_name: Assign Tier 2 Medium Usage Rate for 501 to 1000 Units
rules.rule_description: When a customer's usage units consumed in the billing period are between 501 and 1000 (inclusive), the system assigns the Tier 2 medium-usage per-unit billing rate of $0.45. This rate will be used to calculate the total usage charge for the invoice.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Assign Rate = $0.45 per unit
Tier 2 - Medium Usage

acceptance_criteria.Given: A customer usage record has been read with a valid Units Consumed value, and the billing rate calculation process has been initiated for that customer
acceptance_criteria.When: The Units Consumed in the billing period is greater than 500 units AND less than or equal to 1000 units
acceptance_criteria.Then: The per-unit billing rate is set to $0.45 (Tier 2 - Medium Usage), and the system proceeds to calculate the Usage Charge using this rate

rules.rule_name: Assign Tier 3 High Usage Rate for More Than 1000 Units
rules.rule_description: When a customer's usage units consumed in the billing period exceed 1000 units, the system assigns the Tier 3 high-usage per-unit billing rate of $0.40. This is the lowest per-unit rate and rewards high-volume consumption. This rate will be used to calculate the total usage charge for the invoice.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Assign Rate = $0.40 per unit
Tier 3 - High Usage
More than 1000 units

acceptance_criteria.Given: A customer usage record has been read with a valid Units Consumed value, and the billing rate calculation process has been initiated for that customer
acceptance_criteria.When: The Units Consumed in the billing period is greater than 1000 units
acceptance_criteria.Then: The per-unit billing rate is set to $0.40 (Tier 3 - High Usage), and the system proceeds to calculate the Usage Charge using this rate

rules.rule_name: Calculate Usage Charge from Units and Assigned Rate
rules.rule_description: Once the appropriate tiered per-unit billing rate has been determined based on the customer's units consumed, the system computes the total Usage Charge by multiplying the total units consumed by the assigned per-unit rate. This Usage Charge forms the base amount before any discounts or taxes are applied.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
End: Rate Assigned
Proceed to Calculate Usage Charge

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Units Consumed for the billing period is known and a per-unit billing rate has been assigned based on the applicable usage tier (Tier 1 at $0.50, Tier 2 at $0.45, or Tier 3 at $0.40)
acceptance_criteria.When: The tiered rate assignment is complete and the system proceeds to compute the Usage Charge
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Usage Charge is calculated as Units Consumed multiplied by the assigned per-unit Rate, and this Usage Charge value is carried forward as the base amount for subsequent discount and tax calculations

key_functionalities.title: Calculate Usage Charge
key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    A([Start: Calculate Usage Charge])
    B[Retrieve Total Units Consumed\nfrom Usage Record]
    C[Retrieve Applicable Per-Unit Rate\nas Determined by Usage Tier]
    D[Compute Gross Usage Charge\nTotal Units × Per-Unit Rate]
    E[Store Gross Usage Charge\nfor Discount Processing]
    F([End: Gross Usage Charge Calculated])

    A --> B
    B --> C
    C --> D
    D --> E
    E --> F

rules.rule_name: Compute Gross Usage Charge from Units and Rate
rules.rule_description: The gross usage charge is calculated by multiplying the total units consumed in the billing period by the applicable per-unit rate that was determined based on the usage tier. The resulting gross usage charge is stored for subsequent discount processing.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Compute Gross Usage Charge
Total Units × Per-Unit Rate

acceptance_criteria.Given: A usage record has been read containing the total units consumed for the billing period, and the applicable per-unit rate has already been determined based on the usage tier (either $0.50 for up to 500 units, $0.45 for 501–1000 units, or $0.40 for over 1000 units)
acceptance_criteria.When: The billing system computes the gross usage charge by multiplying the total units consumed (WS-USAGE-UNITS) by the applicable per-unit rate (WS-RATE)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The gross usage charge (WS-USAGE-CHARGE) is set to the product of total units consumed multiplied by the per-unit rate, and this gross usage charge value is retained and made available for all subsequent discount and tax calculations

rules.rule_name: Retrieve Total Units Consumed from Usage Record
rules.rule_description: Before computing the gross usage charge, the total units consumed by the customer during the billing period must be retrieved from the usage record that was read from the Usage File.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Retrieve Total Units Consumed
from Usage Record

acceptance_criteria.Given: A usage record has been successfully read from the Usage File for a customer in a given billing month
acceptance_criteria.When: The billing system prepares to calculate the bill for that customer
acceptance_criteria.Then: The total units consumed (USAGE-UNITS) from the usage record are captured and stored as the working value (WS-USAGE-UNITS) to be used in the gross usage charge computation

rules.rule_name: Retrieve Applicable Per-Unit Rate Based on Usage Tier
rules.rule_description: The per-unit rate to be applied for billing is determined by evaluating which usage tier the customer's total units consumed falls into. Three tiers exist with decreasing rates for higher consumption volumes.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Retrieve Applicable Per-Unit Rate
as Determined by Usage Tier

acceptance_criteria.Given: The total units consumed (WS-USAGE-UNITS) for the billing period have been retrieved from the usage record
acceptance_criteria.When: The billing system evaluates the total units consumed against the defined usage tier thresholds
acceptance_criteria.Then: The per-unit rate (WS-RATE) is set as follows: if total units consumed are 500 or fewer, the rate is $0.50 per unit; if total units consumed are between 501 and 1000 inclusive, the rate is $0.45 per unit; if total units consumed exceed 1000, the rate is $0.40 per unit — and this rate is retained for use in the gross usage charge computation

rules.rule_name: Store Gross Usage Charge for Downstream Discount Processing
rules.rule_description: Once the gross usage charge has been computed, it must be preserved as the base amount from which volume discounts, premium customer discounts, minimum charge comparisons, and tax calculations will subsequently be derived.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Store Gross Usage Charge
for Discount Processing

acceptance_criteria.Given: The gross usage charge has been successfully computed as the product of total units consumed and the applicable per-unit rate
acceptance_criteria.When: The billing system completes the gross usage charge computation step
acceptance_criteria.Then: The gross usage charge value (WS-USAGE-CHARGE) is retained in working storage and is available as the input base amount for all subsequent billing steps including volume discount evaluation, premium discount evaluation, minimum charge floor check, tax computation, and final amount calculation

key_functionalities.title: Apply Volume Discount
key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    A([Start: Apply Volume Discount])
    B{Is Units Consumed\ngreater than\n1000 Units?}
    C[Calculate Volume Discount\nDiscount = Usage Charge × 10%]
    D[No Volume Discount Applied\nDiscount Remains Zero]
    E([End: Proceed to\nPremium Customer Discount Check])

    A --> B
    B -->|Yes - Exceeds Volume Threshold| C
    B -->|No - Within Volume Threshold| D
    C --> E
    D --> E

rules.rule_name: Volume Discount Eligibility Check Based on Units Consumed
rules.rule_description: Determines whether a customer qualifies for a volume discount by checking if their usage units consumed in the billing period exceed the volume threshold of 1000 units.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is Units Consumed greater than 1000 Units?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A customer's bill is being calculated and the Usage Charge has already been determined based on the tiered rate pricing
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates whether the customer's Units Consumed is greater than the Volume Threshold of 1000 units
acceptance_criteria.Then: If Units Consumed is greater than 1000 units, the customer is eligible for a Volume Discount and the system proceeds to calculate the discount amount; If Units Consumed is 1000 units or less, no Volume Discount is applied and the Discount amount remains zero, and the system proceeds to the Premium Customer Discount check

rules.rule_name: Volume Discount Amount Calculation at 10% of Usage Charge
rules.rule_description: Calculates the Volume Discount amount as 10% of the Usage Charge for customers whose Units Consumed exceeds the volume threshold of 1000 units.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Calculate Volume Discount
Discount = Usage Charge × 10%

acceptance_criteria.Given: A customer's Units Consumed is greater than 1000 units and the customer has been determined eligible for a Volume Discount, and the Usage Charge has been computed based on the applicable tiered unit rate
acceptance_criteria.When: The system calculates the Volume Discount
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Volume Discount amount is set to 10% of the Usage Charge (Volume Discount = Usage Charge × 10%), and this Discount value is carried forward to the Premium Customer Discount check

key_functionalities.title: Apply Premium Customer Discount
key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    A([Start: Apply Premium Customer Discount])
    B{Is Customer Type\n= PREMIUM?}
    C[Calculate Premium Discount\n5% of Usage Charge]
    D[Add Premium Discount\nto Existing Discount\nNew Discount = Existing Discount + 5% of Usage Charge]
    E([End: Proceed to Apply\nMinimum Charge Rule])
    F([End: Proceed to Apply\nMinimum Charge Rule])

    A --> B
    B -->|Yes - Premium Customer| C
    C --> D
    D --> E
    B -->|No - Standard Customer\nNo Additional Discount Applied| F

rules.rule_name: Identify Premium Customer for Additional Discount Eligibility
rules.rule_description: Determines whether a customer qualifies for the additional premium discount by checking if their customer type is classified as PREMIUM in the Customer Master record.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is Customer Type = PREMIUM?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A customer record has been retrieved from the Customer Master file and the customer has been verified as ACTIVE, and the usage charge has already been calculated for the current billing period
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates the Customer Type field (CUST-TYPE) from the Customer Master record
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the Customer Type equals 'PREMIUM', the customer is eligible for an additional premium discount and the system proceeds to calculate the premium discount amount; if the Customer Type is any value other than 'PREMIUM' (i.e., standard customer), no additional premium discount is applied and the system proceeds directly to the Minimum Charge Rule evaluation with the discount amount unchanged

rules.rule_name: Calculate and Accumulate Premium Customer Discount
rules.rule_description: For customers classified as PREMIUM, calculates an additional discount based on the Premium Discount Rate applied to the Usage Charge, and adds this premium discount on top of any volume discount that may have already been applied, resulting in a cumulative total discount.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Calculate Premium Discount
5% of Usage Charge
Add Premium Discount to Existing Discount
New Discount = Existing Discount + 5% of Usage Charge

acceptance_criteria.Given: The customer type is confirmed as 'PREMIUM', the Usage Charge (WS-USAGE-CHARGE) has been computed based on usage units and the applicable tiered rate, and the existing discount amount (WS-DISCOUNT) may already contain a volume discount value (which could be zero if the volume threshold was not exceeded)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system calculates the premium discount by multiplying the Usage Charge by the Premium Discount Rate (WS-PREMIUM-DISCOUNT-RATE), and adds the resulting premium discount amount to the existing discount
acceptance_criteria.Then: The total discount (WS-DISCOUNT) is updated to equal the sum of the prior existing discount plus the premium discount amount (Usage Charge × Premium Discount Rate), ensuring that a PREMIUM customer who also exceeded the volume threshold receives both the volume discount and the premium discount cumulatively; the updated total discount is then carried forward to the Minimum Charge Rule evaluation

key_functionalities.title: Apply Minimum Charge Rule
key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    A([Start: Apply Minimum Charge Rule])
    B[Calculate Net Charge\nUsage Charge minus Total Discounts]
    C{Is Net Charge\nless than\nMinimum Charge of $25.00?}
    D[Set Taxable Amount\nto Minimum Charge\n$25.00]
    E[Set Taxable Amount\nto Net Charge\nUsage Charge minus Discounts]
    F([End: Taxable Amount Determined])

    A --> B
    B --> C
    C -->|Yes - Below Minimum| D
    C -->|No - At or Above Minimum| E
    D --> F
    E --> F

rules.rule_name: Apply Minimum Charge Floor When Net Charge Falls Below $25.00
rules.rule_description: When the usage charge after all applicable discounts (volume and/or premium) is less than the system minimum charge of $25.00, the taxable amount must be set to the minimum charge of $25.00 to ensure the customer is always billed at least the minimum amount.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is Net Charge less than Minimum Charge of $25.00?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A customer's usage charge has been calculated and all applicable discounts (volume discount and/or premium discount) have been applied, resulting in a net charge (Usage Charge minus Total Discounts) that is less than the minimum charge of $25.00
acceptance_criteria.When: The billing system evaluates whether the net charge (Usage Charge minus Total Discounts) is less than the minimum charge of $25.00
acceptance_criteria.Then: The taxable amount is set to the minimum charge of $25.00, overriding the discounted net charge, so that the customer is billed no less than $25.00 before tax and previous balance are applied

rules.rule_name: Use Net Charge as Taxable Amount When At or Above Minimum Charge of $25.00
rules.rule_description: When the usage charge after all applicable discounts (volume and/or premium) is equal to or greater than the minimum charge of $25.00, the taxable amount is set to the actual discounted net charge, reflecting the true billable amount before tax.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Set Taxable Amount to Net Charge - Usage Charge minus Discounts

acceptance_criteria.Given: A customer's usage charge has been calculated and all applicable discounts (volume discount and/or premium discount) have been applied, resulting in a net charge (Usage Charge minus Total Discounts) that is equal to or greater than the minimum charge of $25.00
acceptance_criteria.When: The billing system evaluates whether the net charge (Usage Charge minus Total Discounts) is less than the minimum charge of $25.00 and determines it is not
acceptance_criteria.Then: The taxable amount is set to the net charge, calculated as Usage Charge minus Total Discounts, and this amount is used as the base for tax calculation

rules.rule_name: Calculate Net Charge as Basis for Minimum Charge Comparison
rules.rule_description: Before applying the minimum charge rule, the net charge must be derived by subtracting all accumulated discounts (volume discount and premium discount, if applicable) from the gross usage charge. This net charge is the value compared against the minimum charge threshold of $25.00.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Calculate Net Charge - Usage Charge minus Total Discounts

acceptance_criteria.Given: A customer's gross usage charge has been computed based on usage units and the applicable tiered rate, and all eligible discounts (volume discount and/or premium customer discount) have been accumulated into the total discount amount
acceptance_criteria.When: The billing system prepares to determine the taxable amount by evaluating the minimum charge rule
acceptance_criteria.Then: The net charge is derived as Usage Charge minus Total Discounts, and this net charge value is used as the input to the minimum charge comparison to determine whether the minimum charge floor of $25.00 should be applied

key_functionalities.title: Calculate Tax
key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    A([Start: Calculate Tax])
    B[Retrieve Taxable Amount\nAmount after Discounts & Minimum Charge Rule]
    C[Retrieve Customer's Individual Tax Rate\nfrom Customer Record]
    D[Compute Tax Amount\nTax = Taxable Amount × Customer Tax Rate]
    E([End: Tax Amount Determined])

    A --> B
    B --> C
    C --> D
    D --> E

rules.rule_name: Compute Tax Amount Using Customer-Specific Tax Rate
rules.rule_description: The tax amount for a customer's bill is calculated by multiplying the taxable amount (the amount after all discounts and minimum charge rules have been applied) by the customer's individual tax rate retrieved from the Customer Master Record.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Compute Tax Amount
Tax = Taxable Amount × Customer Tax Rate

acceptance_criteria.Given: A customer's taxable amount has been determined (after applying usage charges, discounts, and the minimum charge floor rule), AND the customer's individual tax rate is available from the Customer Master Record
acceptance_criteria.When: The billing system calculates the tax for the current billing period
acceptance_criteria.Then: The tax amount must be computed as: Tax Amount = Taxable Amount × Customer's Individual Tax Rate, AND the resulting Tax Amount is stored for inclusion in the final bill amount

rules.rule_name: Customer Tax Rate is Individually Assigned Per Customer
rules.rule_description: Each customer has their own unique tax rate stored in their Customer Master Record. The tax rate used for billing is not a universal or system-wide rate — it is specific to each individual customer and must be retrieved from that customer's record before tax can be calculated.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Retrieve Customer's Individual Tax Rate
from Customer Record

acceptance_criteria.Given: A usage record is being processed for a specific customer who has been found in the Customer Master File and whose status is ACTIVE
acceptance_criteria.When: The billing system prepares to calculate the tax amount for the customer's bill
acceptance_criteria.Then: The tax rate applied must be the customer's own individual tax rate (CUST-TAX-RATE) as stored in that customer's record in the Customer Master File, NOT a shared or system-level tax rate

rules.rule_name: Taxable Amount Feeds Into Tax Calculation
rules.rule_description: The base amount used for tax calculation is the taxable amount, which is the net charge after all applicable discounts have been subtracted from the usage charge, and after the minimum charge floor rule has been enforced. This ensures tax is never calculated on a raw usage charge but always on the final adjusted billable amount.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Retrieve Taxable Amount
Amount after Discounts & Minimum Charge Rule

acceptance_criteria.Given: The usage charge has been calculated based on the customer's units consumed and the applicable tiered rate, AND all applicable discounts (volume discount and/or premium customer discount) have been applied, AND the minimum charge floor rule has been evaluated
acceptance_criteria.When: The taxable amount is retrieved as the input for tax computation
acceptance_criteria.Then: The taxable amount used as the basis for tax calculation must be either: (a) the result of Usage Charge minus Total Discount, if that result is greater than or equal to the Minimum Charge, OR (b) the Minimum Charge value, if Usage Charge minus Total Discount falls below the Minimum Charge — and this taxable amount is then multiplied by the customer's individual tax rate to produce the Tax Amount

key_functionalities.title: Calculate Final Invoice Amount
key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    A([Start: Calculate Final Invoice Amount])
    B[Retrieve Taxable Amount\nAmount after discounts and minimum charge rule]
    C[Retrieve Calculated Tax Amount\nTaxable Amount × Customer Tax Rate]
    D[Retrieve Customer Previous Outstanding Balance\nFrom Customer Record]
    E[Sum All Components\nTaxable Amount + Tax Amount + Previous Balance]
    F[/Total Amount Due\nFinal Invoice Amount/]
    G([End: Final Invoice Amount Determined])

    A --> B
    B --> C
    C --> D
    D --> E
    E --> F
    F --> G

rules.rule_name: Retrieve Taxable Amount as Input to Final Invoice Calculation
rules.rule_description: The taxable amount, which has already been determined after applying all applicable discounts and enforcing the minimum charge rule, is used as the primary base component when calculating the final invoice amount.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Retrieve Taxable Amount
Amount after discounts and minimum charge rule

acceptance_criteria.Given: A billing calculation is in progress for an active customer and the taxable amount has already been determined (either as Usage Charge minus Total Discount, or as the Minimum Charge if the net charge fell below the minimum threshold)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system is ready to compute the final total amount due on the invoice
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must use the previously computed Taxable Amount (WS-TAXABLE-AMOUNT) as the first component in the final invoice amount calculation, ensuring it reflects all prior discount and minimum charge adjustments

rules.rule_name: Retrieve Calculated Tax Amount as Input to Final Invoice Calculation
rules.rule_description: The tax amount, which has been individually calculated for the customer using their specific tax rate applied to the taxable amount, is used as the second component when computing the final invoice total.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Retrieve Calculated Tax Amount
Taxable Amount × Customer Tax Rate

acceptance_criteria.Given: A billing calculation is in progress for an active customer and the tax amount has already been computed as Taxable Amount multiplied by the customer's individual tax rate (CUST-TAX-RATE) sourced from the Customer Master record
acceptance_criteria.When: The system is ready to compute the final total amount due on the invoice
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must use the previously computed Tax Amount (WS-TAX) as the second additive component in the final invoice amount calculation, ensuring the customer-specific tax rate has been applied

rules.rule_name: Retrieve Customer Previous Outstanding Balance from Customer Record
rules.rule_description: The customer's previous outstanding balance, as stored in the Customer Master record, is carried forward and included in the current invoice total to ensure any unpaid prior amounts are collected in the current billing cycle.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Retrieve Customer Previous Outstanding Balance
From Customer Record

acceptance_criteria.Given: A billing calculation is in progress for an active customer and the Customer Master record for that customer has been located and loaded, containing the field CUST-PREV-BALANCE representing any outstanding balance from prior billing periods
acceptance_criteria.When: The system is ready to compute the final total amount due on the invoice
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must retrieve the Previous Outstanding Balance (CUST-PREV-BALANCE) directly from the Customer Master record and include it as the third additive component in the final invoice amount calculation

rules.rule_name: Compute Final Invoice Amount by Summing All Billing Components
rules.rule_description: The final total amount due on the customer's invoice is calculated by summing three components: the taxable amount (after discounts and minimum charge), the tax amount (based on the customer's tax rate), and the customer's previous outstanding balance. This produces the definitive amount the customer owes for the current billing period.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Sum All Components
Taxable Amount + Tax Amount + Previous Balance

acceptance_criteria.Given: An active customer's billing calculation has been completed, producing: (1) a Taxable Amount (WS-TAXABLE-AMOUNT) after all discounts and minimum charge rules have been applied, (2) a Tax Amount (WS-TAX) computed as Taxable Amount multiplied by the customer's individual tax rate from the Customer Master record, and (3) a Previous Outstanding Balance (CUST-PREV-BALANCE) retrieved from the Customer Master record
acceptance_criteria.When: The system computes the final invoice amount
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must calculate the Final Invoice Amount (WS-FINAL-AMOUNT) using the formula: Final Amount = Taxable Amount + Tax Amount + Previous Outstanding Balance, and this computed value must be stored as the total amount due to be included on the generated invoice

key_functionalities.title: Generate Invoice Number
key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    A([Start: Generate Invoice Number])
    B[Clear Invoice Number Field]
    C[Take Billing Month\nfrom Usage Record]
    D[Take Customer ID\nfrom Customer Record]
    E[Combine: Billing Month + '-' + Customer ID]
    F[/Invoice Number Created\ne.g. 2024-01 - CUST001/]
    G([End: Invoice Number Ready])

    A --> B
    B --> C
    C --> D
    D --> E
    E --> F
    F --> G

rules.rule_name: Clear Invoice Number Before Construction
rules.rule_description: Before generating a new invoice number, the invoice number field must be cleared of any previously held value to ensure no residual data contaminates the new invoice number.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Clear Invoice Number Field

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Generate Invoice process has been triggered for a customer's usage record
acceptance_criteria.When: The system begins constructing a new invoice number
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Invoice Number field must be reset to blank/empty spaces before any new value is assigned, ensuring no carry-over data from a previously processed invoice exists in the field

rules.rule_name: Invoice Number Source - Billing Month from Usage Record
rules.rule_description: The billing month used in the invoice number must be sourced directly from the current usage record being processed, ensuring the invoice number reflects the correct billing period.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Take Billing Month from Usage Record

acceptance_criteria.Given: A usage record has been read and is currently being processed
acceptance_criteria.When: The system constructs the invoice number
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Billing Month component of the invoice number must be taken from the Billing Month field (WS-BILLING-MONTH) of the current usage record, which was captured when the usage record was read

rules.rule_name: Invoice Number Source - Customer ID from Customer Record
rules.rule_description: The customer identifier used in the invoice number must be sourced from the matched Customer Master record, ensuring the invoice number is tied to the correct customer account.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Take Customer ID from Customer Record

acceptance_criteria.Given: A matching customer record has been found in the Customer Master file for the current usage record
acceptance_criteria.When: The system constructs the invoice number
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Customer ID component of the invoice number must be taken from the Customer ID field (CUST-ID) of the matched Customer Master record

rules.rule_name: Invoice Number Construction by Combining Billing Month and Customer ID
rules.rule_description: A unique invoice number is constructed by concatenating the billing month, a hyphen separator, and the customer ID. This ensures each invoice can be uniquely identified by its billing period and customer.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Combine: Billing Month + '-' + Customer ID

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Billing Month has been taken from the current usage record and the Customer ID has been taken from the matched Customer Master record
acceptance_criteria.When: The system generates the invoice number
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Invoice Number must be formed by concatenating: Billing Month value + literal hyphen character '-' + Customer ID value, in that exact order, with no additional separators or spaces between components (e.g., '2024-01-CUST001')

rules.rule_name: Invoice Number Uniqueness Per Customer Per Billing Month
rules.rule_description: The resulting invoice number uniquely identifies a billing event for a specific customer in a specific billing month. The combination of billing month and customer ID guarantees uniqueness of each invoice within a billing cycle.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Invoice Number Created e.g. 2024-01 - CUST001

acceptance_criteria.Given: A usage record exists for a customer with a specific billing month, and a matching active customer record exists in the Customer Master
acceptance_criteria.When: The invoice number is fully constructed
acceptance_criteria.Then: The resulting Invoice Number must be a unique identifier in the format '[Billing Month]-[Customer ID]' (e.g., '2024-01-CUST001'), where the Billing Month comes from the usage record and the Customer ID comes from the Customer Master record, and this invoice number is then used to identify the invoice record written to the Invoice output file

acceptance_criteria.Given: A usage charge amount has been calculated for the customer based on their consumed units and the applicable tiered rate
acceptance_criteria.When: The invoice output is being prepared for the current billing period
acceptance_criteria.Then: The usage charge value is formatted into a display-ready field (WS-DISPLAY-CHARGE) suitable for inclusion in the invoice record, preserving the monetary value accurately for customer-facing output

rules.rule_name: Format Discount Amount for Invoice Display

acceptance_criteria.Given: A total discount amount has been determined for the customer, which may reflect a volume discount, a premium customer discount, or a combination of both, or zero if no discounts apply
acceptance_criteria.When: The invoice output is being prepared for the current billing period
acceptance_criteria.Then: The total discount value is formatted into a display-ready field (WS-DISPLAY-DISCOUNT) suitable for inclusion in the invoice record, showing the customer the total savings applied to their bill

rules.rule_name: Format Tax Amount for Invoice Display
rules.rule_description: The tax amount calculated on the customer's taxable amount using the customer-specific tax rate must be converted into a display-ready format before being printed on the invoice record.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Format Tax Amount into Display-Ready Value

acceptance_criteria.Given: A tax amount has been calculated by applying the customer's individual tax rate to the taxable amount (which is either the net charge after discounts or the minimum charge floor, whichever is greater)
acceptance_criteria.When: The invoice output is being prepared for the current billing period
acceptance_criteria.Then: The tax amount value is formatted into a display-ready field (WS-DISPLAY-TAX) suitable for inclusion in the invoice record, providing the customer with a transparent view of the tax component of their bill

rules.rule_name: Format Previous Balance for Invoice Display
rules.rule_description: The customer's outstanding previous balance carried forward from prior billing periods must be converted into a display-ready format before being printed on the invoice record.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Format Previous Balance into Display-Ready Value

acceptance_criteria.Given: A previous balance amount exists on the customer's account as retrieved from the Customer Master record (CUST-PREV-BALANCE), which may be zero if the account is fully paid
acceptance_criteria.When: The invoice output is being prepared for the current billing period
acceptance_criteria.Then: The previous balance value is formatted into a display-ready field (WS-DISPLAY-BALANCE) suitable for inclusion in the invoice record, clearly showing the customer any outstanding amount carried forward from prior periods

rules.rule_name: Format Total Amount Due for Invoice Display
rules.rule_description: The final total amount due, which is the sum of the taxable amount, tax, and any previous outstanding balance, must be converted into a display-ready format before being printed on the invoice record as the customer's total payment obligation.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Format Total Amount Due into Display-Ready Value

acceptance_criteria.Given: A final total amount due has been computed for the customer as the sum of the taxable amount (net charge after discounts or minimum charge), the tax amount, and the previous balance carried forward
acceptance_criteria.When: The invoice output is being prepared for the current billing period
acceptance_criteria.Then: The final total amount value is formatted into a display-ready field (WS-DISPLAY-TOTAL) suitable for inclusion in the invoice record, representing the complete amount the customer is required to pay for the current billing period including all charges, taxes, and prior balances

acceptance_criteria.When: The system writes the invoice record
